name: Super-Kamiokande-IV solar-neutrino measurement (full data period)
notes: key_value and key_value_text numbers were re-checked against the text of the paper (arXiv:2312.12907) on 2026-10-25 and match.

summary.plain: Super-Kamiokande measured the flux of boron-8 solar neutrinos using the full period of its fourth phase, SK-IV (2,970 days), and combined it with the earlier phases (5,805 live days in total). The paper also reports the solar neutrino oscillation parameters obtained from all solar experiments.
summary.technical: Combines SK-I through SK-IV (5,805 live days total); SK-IV alone contributes 2,970 days (Oct. 2008 - May 2018) and 65,443 +390/−388 (stat.) ± 925 (syst.) solar-neutrino events. 8B flux (2.314 ± 0.014 ± 0.040)×10⁶ cm⁻² s⁻¹ for SK-IV (assuming no neutrino oscillations) and (2.336 ± 0.011 ± 0.043)×10⁶ cm⁻² s⁻¹ combined with all SK phases up to SK-IV. From all solar experiments including SK's 5805-day data set, sin²θ12 = 0.306 ± 0.013 and Δm²21 = (6.10 +0.95 −0.81)×10⁻⁵ eV², a deviation of about 1.5σ from the Δm²21 obtained by KamLAND.

title: Solar neutrino measurements using the full data period of Super-Kamiokande-IV
why_it_matters: The paper tests for an energy-dependent 'upturn' of the electron-neutrino survival probability (from about 0.3 at high energy, above 10 MeV, to about 0.6 at low energy, below 1 MeV) and reports a solar Δm²21 that deviates by about 1.5σ from the KamLAND value.
